discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computing and quantum simulation with trapped ions and ultracold atoms

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / quantum information and quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed how controllable atomic systems can process quantum information and simulate quantum matter. Their 1995 proposal for a trapped-ion quantum computer, with entangling gates mediated by collective motion, gave the first realistic blueprint for scalable quantum logic and was soon realized in the laboratory. It still underlies today's ion-trap processors. With Jaksch and others, they proposed realizing the Bose-Hubbard model with ultracold atoms in optical lattices and predicted the superfluid-Mott insulator transition. This work began the field of analog quantum simulation, which now probes quantum magnetism, topology, localization and thermalization. They also developed key ideas for quantum networks, quantum repeaters, Rydberg-atom gates and tensor-network descriptions of many-body states. Rarely have theoretical proposals been so concrete or so reliably confirmed by experiment. Their work now defines the atomic, molecular and optical approach to quantum technology.
